newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonian PM reshuffles government amid crisis.
newsitem.headline: Macedonian PM reshuffles government amid crisis.

text.p: Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski carried out a major reshuffle of his cabinet amid a deepening political and economic crisis caused by the collapse of a pyramid savings scheme.
The shakeup, revealed late on Tuesday, brought in nine new ministers and three new deputy premiers. The new line-up is expected to receive a vote of confidence in parliament, analysts said.
Faced with major financial scandal and accusations of corruption in the highest levels of the government two months ago, Crvenkovski had promised a major cabinet reshuffle.

Construction Minister Jorgo Sundovski resigned because of his involvment in the pyramid financial institution TAT, followed by Health Minister Ilija Filipce who was accused of corruption and criminal negligence.

Crvenkovski fired two of the most prominent reformist ministers -- Jane Miljovski, who was deputy prime minister and vice-president of the ruling SDAM party, and Foreign Minister Ljubomir Frckoski, one of the authors of the Macedonian democratic constitution.
He also brought in a new economy minister, Boris Rikalovski, to replace Becir Zuta (PDP), but kept Taki Fiti as finance minister.

Crvenkovski is expected to announce early elections this autumn after negotiations with opposition political parties, one of which has already announced a series of protest rallies across the country starting on Wednesday calling for the premier to quit and new elections as soon as possible.
Diplomats saw the changes as a defeat for reformist faction in Macedonian politics and the return of neo-communist politicians to the scene.

The ruling coalition consists of the Social Democratic Alliance (SDAM), the Socialist Party (SP) and the ethnic Albanian Party of Democratic Prosperity (PDP), and holds a two-thirds majority in parliament.
New defence minister is Lazar Kitanovski, replacing Blagoj Handziski who takes over from Frckoski as foreign minister.
Former Macedonian ambassador to Bulgaria Gjorgi Spasov takes over the Justice ministry from Vlado Popovski. Tomislav Cokreski remains interior minister.
